source_name: Municipal 'közérdekű adatok / közbeszerzés' disclosure pages (e.g. Érd MJV, Budapest XIII. IMFK)
why_relevant: Statutory per-buyer disclosure pages carrying procurement plans, procedure lists and contract data for individual municipalities and their institution-operating companies — the granular layer where small account/POS contracts actually surface.

source_subtype: corporate supplier portal / vendor onboarding hub
why_relevant: Landing hub of Hungary's largest bank for vendors; links new-partner prequalification, SAP Ariba onboarding and the OTP Partner Code of Ethics. Sole public front door into OTP Group sourcing, which never appears on public procurement portals.

source_name: OTP Bank – Legyen Ön is partnerünk! (new supplier self-registration)
why_relevant: Documents the actual entry mechanism: download self-registration form, send to vendorman@otpbank.hu, prequalification review, then registration into the potential-supplier pool. This is the operational route a vendor must take to be invited to OTP sourcing events.

Confirms OTP runs sourcing events, POs and confirmations through SAP Ariba Network (Standard account free for suppliers), rolled out gradually. Identifies the e-sourcing platform that carries OTP's RFx traffic — critical for understanding how/where OTP tenders actually surface.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H.) – group procurement arm
source_subtype: group procurement entity page + supplier document library
why_relevant: The legal/organisational owner of Erste Bank Hungary's external spend. Publishes supplier general documents (NDA, supplier audit questionnaire, performance and sustainability scorecards) and a partner whistleblower channel — i.e. the actual vendor-onboarding paperwork a supplier to the Hungarian bank must sign. Subsidiaries exist in Hungary per group descriptions.

Referenced by Erste Group as the procurement unit's own website; the likely host of the online procurement platform / supplier entry point used for Erste Bank Hungary sourcing. Not fetched in this pass — URL recorded for the deterministic liveness pass.

source_subtype: CSR/procurement policy page with spend and supplier statistics
why_relevant: CIB (Intesa Sanpaolo group) states its procurement principle of transparent selection via bidding and negotiation, uniform conditions and contractual ethics obligations aligned to ISP guidelines; discloses supplier counts (2,907 suppliers, 2,807 Hungarian) and ~HUF 22.9bn services spend. Rare quantified view of a Hungarian private bank's addressable vendor spend.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. – Áruk és szolgáltatások beszerzésének általános feltételei (procurement GTC, PDF)
why_relevant: Published general terms and conditions governing Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. and its subsidiaries' purchases of goods and services — the contractual framework any supplier is held to. One of the few Hungarian bank procurement documents published as a standalone public PDF.
Document hub where the procurement GTC and related corporate documents are published; the practical way to detect newly posted or revised procurement-side documents for Raiffeisen Hungary.

source_name: K&H Csoport fenntarthatósági irányelvek (sustainability policy, incl. responsible procurement)
why_relevant: Closest thing found to a public K&H (KBC group) procurement policy: describes the CSR declaration built into all supplier contracts since 2010 (ethics, environment, anti-corruption, human rights) and KBC group blacklist constraints on counterparties. K&H publishes no supplier portal, so this document is the primary public window on its vendor requirements.

source_name: MBH Bank Nyrt. – Etikai Kódex (Code of Ethics, procurement chapter)
why_relevant: MBH publishes no supplier portal; its Code of Ethics is the only located public statement of sourcing conduct, confirming that larger purchases run through a bidding process (pályáztatás) and setting impartiality rules for staff dealing with vendors. Establishes that competitive RFx exists at MBH even though it is never publicly advertised.
MBH's regulated-document repository; the practical monitoring point for any future supplier/procurement document appearing at Hungary's second-largest bank, which currently has no vendor-facing page.

A UniCredit Hungary 'partnerkapu' (partner gate) sub-site with downloadable documents surfaced in Hungarian search. Its exact scope (whether it covers vendor partners or only business-intermediary partners) was not confirmed in this pass — worth verifying because UniCredit publishes no other Hungarian vendor-facing channel.

source_name: MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank – Közbeszerzési eljárások (közzétételi lista)
source_subtype: public procurement disclosure list of a state bank
why_relevant: MFB is a state-owned bank and therefore a contracting authority: it publishes full EKR summaries (összegezés) naming winners, prices and lot scope for banking IT and licence buys (e.g. an Atlassian licence procedure). Because Hungarian private banks buy comparable categories invisibly, MFB's published awards are the best public price/vendor benchmark for the same category basket.

Hungary's national e-procurement system. Private banks are not contracting authorities, but they appear in EKR as ajánlattevő (bidder) — e.g. MBH Bank, OTP and Gránit in the MFB Pont Plusz consortium procedure. Searching EKR by bank name reveals where these banks sell into the state and, indirectly, which delivery partners they field.

Official gazette and searchable document store for Hungarian procurement notices and contract documents (kereso-core.kozbeszerzes.hu hosts contract PDFs). Used to trace bank names appearing as bidders/winners and to benchmark the same IT/facility/card-personalisation categories private banks buy privately.

source_name: MNB törzsadat-bejelentés jogszabály (58/2015. MNB rendelet) és Intézménykereső / ERA
why_relevant: The master-data reporting regime (58/2015. MNB rendelet, submitted via the ERA portal) and the public institution search let you resolve exact legal entity identities of all banks in this cell and detect subsidiaries/outsourcing entities that are the real contracting parties for supplier deals.

source_name: OTP Bank – Fenntarthatósági jelentések / ESG (integrált éves jelentés)
why_relevant: OTP reports sustainability (and from 2022 procurement-relevant ESG content) inside the Integrated Annual Report. These reports are where supplier counts, local-sourcing share and supplier ESG-screening practices surface for the largest Hungarian buyer — data never present on the supplier portal itself.

OTP runs sourcing on SAP Ariba. Private-sector buyers can push RFx as public Discovery postings; monitoring Discovery for Hungarian financial-services buyers is the only route by which an OTP-type private RFP can become externally visible without an invitation.

source_name: OPTEN / Nemzeti Cégtár – company registry data on bank entities and their suppliers
why_relevant: Registry data (company IDs, ownership, financials) for both the buying banks and candidate suppliers; needed to resolve which legal entity signs vendor contracts (e.g. GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt., Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. cg. 01-10-041042) and to size suppliers that win bank work.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – Visszaélés-bejelentő rendszer az Erste Csoport partnerei számára
why_relevant: Partner/supplier-facing whistleblowing channel — confirms the existence of a formal supplier-relationship compliance layer at Erste Bank Hungary and is a leading indicator of supplier-governance changes (a channel like this is usually created alongside supplier code enforcement).

Hungarian procurement trade portal that surfaced repeatedly on supplier-qualification queries; useful for local vocabulary, prevailing supplier-qualification practice, and for identifying procurement leaders/consultancies serving Hungarian banks — a snowballing route to named procurement contacts.

source_name: Magyar Telekom beszerzési portál (szállítói regisztráció) – structural comparator
why_relevant: Not a bank, but the reference implementation of a fully public Hungarian corporate supplier portal (versenyfelhívások = published RFx, szállítói regisztráció, működési kódex, named lead buyers). It defines the Hungarian vocabulary and the structural template to look for at banks, and shows exactly what Hungarian banks do NOT publish.
Nordic core/card vendor that publicly announced completing OTP Bank Hungary's card acquiring software replacement; its newsroom is a de-facto award notice channel for Hungarian card-processing deals.

source_name: Oracle corporate press releases (Financial Services / FLEXCUBE)
why_relevant: Oracle publicly announced MKB Bank Hungary's full FLEXCUBE core banking transformation; Oracle FS press releases are a primary award-notice substitute for large private-sector core deals.

Announced OTP Bank Hungary's selection of Intellect Digital Core for retail/SME core banking — the single largest Hungarian core-banking vendor win of recent years, disclosed by the seller not the buyer.

Euronet operates a large share of Hungary's ATM estate and announces ATM outsourcing / bank-branded ATM deals (e.g. taking over 100+ ATMs for ABN AMRO Hungary). Investor-relations releases are contractually disciplined and datable.
